=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer-Side Review of Seller Draft

**Preliminary flag:** The Seller's framing ("FINAL," "not to be re-opened," "settled at principal level," "standard and widely accepted") is negotiation pressure, not a binding constraint. There is no evidence your principals agreed these terms. Treat every item as open. Several Seller positions also create a circular trap: broad general disclosure + buyer-knowledge bar + 18-month limits on *everything* would gut the warranty package precisely where the data room reveals live problems (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the privacy incident).

---

**SPA-N-001 — General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% of price = AUD 4.8m.
- *Buyer wants:* Higher comfort; 20% is at the top of Seller's own cited range. Push toward 25–30% for general warranties, with fundamentals at 100%.
- *Recommendation:* **Negotiate up / accept ~20% only if fundamentals are carved to 100%** — a single cap across all warranties under-protects on title and tax.

**SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket (excess-only/tipping from the top).
- *Buyer wants:* Basket ~1% (AUD 240k) is acceptable, but prefer a **first-dollar "deductible that tips"** so you recover from dollar one once the basket is reached, not just the excess.
- *Recommendation:* **Accept thresholds but convert basket to tipping-basket (full recovery once exceeded).** — Excess-only recovery is a hidden second deductible.

**SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; and a default that *all* claims share this limit "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- *Buyer wants:* 18–24 months is defensible for general warranties, but tax should run to the statutory limitation period (typically 7 years) and fundamentals longer.
- *Recommendation:* **Accept ~18–24 months for general only; reject the "applies to all claims" default.** — The catch-all silently shortens tax and title protection.

**SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity/title subject to *same* cap and time limits as general, "for administrative simplicity."
- *Buyer wants:* Title and capacity at **100% of price, long/unlimited time limit** — these go to whether you actually acquire the asset.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject firmly.** — You are paying AUD 24m; title failure must be recoverable in full, not capped at 4.8m.

**SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* Silent — no fraud/fraudulent misrepresentation carve-out from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provisions.
- *Buyer wants:* All limitations (and non-reliance/exclusive-remedy) **expressly disapplied for fraud, wilful concealment, and fraudulent misrepresentation.**
- *Recommendation:* **Insert an unqualified fraud carve-out.** — Caps and non-reliance clauses must never shelter a dishonest seller.

**SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* Deems disclosed the *entire* data room, Accounts, statutory registers and *all publicly searchable records* (general sweep-up).
- *Buyer wants:* Disclosure limited to matters **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to assess** the matter; no "whole data room / public register" deemed disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject general/deemed disclosure; require a "fairly disclosed" standard and specific disclosures only.** — A dump-everything standard lets known problems defeat warranties.

**SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew or that was *discoverable* from data room/public records.
- *Buyer wants:* Delete. At most, actual knowledge of named deal-team members — never "discoverable" or constructive knowledge.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject, especially "discoverable."** — Combined with SPA-N-006 this is a constructive-knowledge trap that eliminates most warranty claims.

**SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* "Reasonable endeavours"; consent "satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent"; no final consent yet in data room. Bluefen is ~30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m) with change-of-control clause 11.2/11.3 conditions.
- *Buyer wants:* **Bluefen written consent (with all 11.3 conditions satisfied) as a hard Condition Precedent to Completion**, evidenced before close.
- *Recommendation:* **Make it a CP, not a post-completion endeavour.** — Losing a 30%-of-revenue customer on change-of-control destroys deal value.

**SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, change-of-control 8.1, discharge 9.2; "release following Completion," not yet repaid.
- *Buyer wants:* This is **debt** — on a debt-free/cash-free basis it must be repaid/discharged at or before Completion out of Seller proceeds, with deed of release delivered at close.
- *Recommendation:* **Require discharge/payoff at Completion as a CP; adjust funds flow so Seller bears it.** — "Release following Completion" leaves you owning the debt and security risk.

**SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* AUD 420k DD-005 Completion bonuses "a matter for the Seller," not in funds flow; on-costs (payroll tax/super) unstated.
- *Buyer wants:* These are triggered *by Completion* — a pre-completion liability of the Company. **Seller must bear them (plus on-costs) via price/funds-flow adjustment or specific indemnity.**
- *Recommendation:* **Add specific indemnity + funds-flow deduction covering bonuses and all on-costs.** — Debt-free/cash-free means the buyer shouldn't fund the seller's deal bonuses.

**SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment (~AUD 180k open); DD-004 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on *cleared payment of every SOW3 fee*; no proof of payment/assignment in data room.
- *Buyer wants:* **Broader indemnity for failure of IP title/assignment** (not just the payment), plus proof of payment and executed assignment delivered — risk is you don't own the IP, not merely the 180k.
- *Recommendation:* **Expand indemnity to cover IP ownership/assignment failure; require payment evidence + assignment as CP.** — Capping at the fee ignores the real risk: no clear title to Project Materials.

**SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* DD-006 export of ~1,240 records to wrong address; "preliminary," "not expected to be material," no confirmed breach.
- *Buyer wants:* A **specific uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity** covering notification costs, regulator action (OAIC/Privacy Act), remediation and third-party claims; conduct-of-claims rights; and a warranty that there is no other data incident.
- *Recommendation:* **Require a specific indemnity — do not let "preliminary" characterisation plus general disclosure bury it.** — Notifiable Data Breach exposure is real and should not sit under the general cap/knowledge bar.

**SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* 3 related renewals, AUD 110k each (AUD 330k), "ordinary-course operating costs"; terminability/accrual unstated.
- *Buyer wants:* Clarity on whether these are **committed/unavoidable** (then a working-capital/debt-like item) vs genuinely ordinary. Possible related-party angle given they're "related." Confirm no pre-completion lock-in without consent.
- *Recommendation:* **Diligence the three contracts; treat committed spend as a funds-flow/working-capital adjustment and add a no-unusual-commitments warranty.** — "Ordinary course" is asserted, not evidenced.

**SPA-N-014 — Category separation**
- *Seller:* Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to *all Claims of any nature* (9.3/12.8/20.5).
- *Buyer wants:* **Tiered regime** — separate treatment for fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses) and fraud, each outside the general cap/time/knowledge limits.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the blanket application; carve indemnities, tax, fundamentals and fraud out of all limitations.** — A single "all claims" bucket neutralises your most important protections.

**SPA-N-015 — Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced solely by the Company share register (DD-012); notes buyer hasn't done own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Full **title warranty at 100% cap/long limit** (per SPA-N-004) plus independent evidence — ASIC search, original register, no encumbrances/options, Harbourglass's own acquisition chain.
- *Recommendation:* **Do not rely on the register alone; condition close on independent title verification and a 100% title warranty.** — The register is Seller-produced; you need backstopping warranty protection.

**SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* "Settled under the general regime" — i.e., tax and IP warranties get the 20% cap, 18-month limit, knowledge bar and general disclosure.
- *Buyer wants:* **Dedicated tax covenant/indemnity** running to the statutory period (no knowledge qualifier), and IP warranties with robust (ideally higher/longer) treatment given SaaS value is in the IP.
- *Recommendation:* **Negotiate a standalone tax deed and enhanced IP warranty regime outside the general limits.** — Tax and IP are the core risk/value drivers of a SaaS target and shouldn't ride the general cap.

---

**Cross-cutting priorities (what to hold firm on):**
1. Fundamentals/title/tax **out of** the general cap and knowledge bar (SPA-N-004, 014, 016).
2. **Fraud carve-out** (SPA-N-005) — non-negotiable.
3. **Bluefen and Riverlark as CPs** (SPA-N-008, 009) — these affect whether the asset and its revenue survive close.
4. Kill **"discoverable" knowledge + whole-data-room deemed disclosure** (SPA-N-006, 007).
5. **Specific indemnities** for privacy incident, Ironquay IP, and employee bonuses (SPA-N-010, 011, 012).

Want me to draft a mark-up / issues list in SPA clause-reference form for the Seller, or a one-page principal-level summary for your deal lead?
